title: A System, Not a Hero
paragraphs: The legend of penicillin attributes a medical revolution to a single accident, and the attribution is not entirely false. Between them, these two facts frame the whole story. In nineteen twenty eight, Alexander Fleming returned from a holiday to find that a mould had contaminated a staphylococcus culture and that the bacteria around it had died. But an observation is not yet a treatment, and the distance between the two was considerable.

Fleming published his findings in nineteen twenty nine, but his laboratory notebooks are sketchy and his later recollections do not always agree. For roughly a decade he regarded the substance mainly as a possible topical antiseptic, and he did not fully grasp its wider promise. Such caution was not unreasonable for its time, but it delayed progress by years.

The decisive labour fell to others. At Oxford, Howard Florey and Ernst Chain assembled a team that learned to purify the drug, tested it against bacterial disease, and by nineteen forty showed that it could work as a therapy. Norman Heatley, whose extraction methods helped make production practical, belonged to that group too. Without their patient experiments, penicillin might have remained a footnote in a laboratory notebook.

When the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded in nineteen forty five, it was shared by Fleming, Florey and Chain, but not by Heatley. Oxford would not award him an honorary doctorate until nineteen ninety. The omission illustrates a general difficulty: prizes reward identifiable individuals, whereas discoveries are produced by systems.

A more accurate story of penicillin would therefore replace the lone genius with a sequence: an alert observer, a stalled idea, and a team willing to do the unglamorous work. It is a less romantic story, but it is the one that best explains how a curiosity became a medicine.

sources.claim: Fleming 1928'de bir stafilokok kültürünü bulaştıran küfün çevresindeki bakterileri öldürdüğünü gördü; 1929'da yayımladı, laboratuvar defterleri özensiz ve sonraki anlatımları çelişkilidir; yaklaşık on yıl boyunca maddeyi esas olarak yerel antiseptik olarak düşündü.
